School Cleaning Standards

What are school cleaning standards?

School cleaning standards are the hygiene and amenity requirements a school keeps across classrooms, toilets, corridors and canteens – the duties a school documents and a contractor delivers on schedule.

Where the requirements come from

The requirements come from Department of Education guidance, the school's own spec and public health advice – three layers that stack, not one document.

The areas a school clean covers

A school clean covers classrooms, amenities blocks, corridors, gym floors, canteens and admin zones – each with its own frequency and product rules.

The duties a school cleaner carries

A school cleaner's duties run vacuum, mop, sanitise amenities, empty bins and wipe touch points in a set zone order. Responsibilities extend past the mop: the cleaner is the person who sees the campus at its emptiest, so the role quietly absorbs reporting duties too.

What are the 6 basic cleaning steps in a school?

The six steps run wash, wipe, rinse, dry, check and sign – the same surface loop every zone repeats.

Do janitors clean classrooms every day?

Yes – janitors clean classrooms every school day, typically after hours once students and staff have left.

What is a cleaner at a school called?

A school cleaner is called a cleaner, custodian or facilities officer – the title changes, the duty set does not.

How many hours does a school need per week?

A school's weekly hours are set by enrolment and building size – the roster is specified per zone, not bought as a lump; a service provider prices against that roster.

How does a school stay clean between visits?

A school stays clean between visits through tidy routines, lunch supervision, waste systems and spill reporting – the housekeeping layer students and staff own.

Who runs standards-aligned school cleaning in Melbourne?

Whistle Clean runs standards-aligned programs for schools – a rostered crew works to the business manager's brief with a named supervisor and signed visit logs.
